components.name: button
components.description: A native button with explicit type and visual emphasis.
components.accessibility: Uses a real button. Choose type="submit" inside a form; the default button never submits accidentally. Disabled buttons remain native disabled controls. Visible text supplies the accessible name.

components.name: link
components.description: A native navigation link with optional visual emphasis.
components.accessibility: Use meaningful link text. Internal hrefs receive ordinary Portal mount resolution. Do not use this as a fake disabled button.

components.name: badge
components.description: A compact textual status marker.
components.accessibility: Text communicates status; colour and the optional dot are supplementary. This component does not announce changes as a live region.

components.name: card
components.description: A panel with optional header and footer.
components.accessibility: Choose heading levels in caller content to match the page hierarchy; Card does not force an h2 or region label.

components.name: alert
components.description: A static notice with optional heading and actions.
components.accessibility: Static notices do not use role=alert, avoiding unsolicited announcements on page load. Dynamic error announcements require the host runtime contract.

components.name: separator
components.description: A semantic horizontal thematic break.
components.accessibility: Preserve semantic HTML and visible focus styles when customizing.

components.name: container
components.description: A centered content-width container.
components.accessibility: Preserve semantic HTML and visible focus styles when customizing.

components.name: stack
components.description: A vertical or horizontal flex layout with token spacing.
components.accessibility: Preserve semantic HTML and visible focus styles when customizing.

components.name: grid
components.description: A responsive grid that collapses on narrow screens.
components.accessibility: DOM order remains reading and keyboard order. Do not use CSS to change meaningful content order.

components.name: field
components.description: A label, description and error wrapper for an explicitly identified control.
components.accessibility: The for prop must equal the nested control id. Also set required on the control. When using description/error, provide descriptionId/errorId and pass those same ids to the nested control describedby prop (space-separated if both). Mark the control invalid=true for an error. IDs must be unique in the document.

components.name: input
components.description: A native single-line input with label/error association.
components.accessibility: Always provide a visible associated label. Placeholder is not a label. Pass a unique id for each repeated control. File inputs do not gain upload capability from this component.

components.name: textarea
components.description: A native multiline control.
components.accessibility: Always provide a visible associated label. The value is text content, not an HTML value attribute.

components.name: select
components.description: A native select with caller-owned option elements.
components.accessibility: Use option/optgroup elements in the default slot. Set selected on the desired option; the component has no browser-managed value synchronization.

components.name: checkbox
components.description: A native checkbox with an enclosing text label.
components.accessibility: The enclosing label associates text without an id. Group related choices in a caller-owned fieldset with a legend. Radios in a group share a name and have distinct values.

components.name: radio
components.description: A native radio with an enclosing text label.
components.accessibility: The enclosing label associates text without an id. Group related choices in a caller-owned fieldset with a legend. Radios in a group share a name and have distinct values.

components.name: field-error
components.description: An explicitly identified error message for aria-describedby.
components.accessibility: Reference this id in the control describedby prop and mark invalid=true. The error is not a live region by default.

components.name: error-summary
components.description: A focusable validation summary with caller-owned field links.
components.accessibility: Give each summary a unique id if more than one is rendered. Link errors to actual control ids. This markup is focusable but does not automatically move focus; that requires the form/runtime integration.

components.name: disclosure
components.description: Native details/summary disclosure without JavaScript.
components.accessibility: Summary is the native keyboard-operable trigger. Do not place other interactive controls inside summary. Each disclosure is independent; no enforced accordion exclusivity.

components.name: table
components.description: A semantic table with caption and caller-owned header/body rows.
components.accessibility: Use tr elements in slots and appropriate th scope attributes. The caption is visible. The labelled wrapper is keyboard-focusable so overflowing columns can be scrolled with arrow keys. No sorting, row selection or grid keyboard model is implied.

components.name: breadcrumbs
components.description: A labelled breadcrumb navigation list.
components.accessibility: Supply li items. Mark the current page with aria-current=page and use text rather than a redundant active link. Separators are decorative CSS.

components.name: pagination
components.description: A labelled container for page navigation.
components.accessibility: Supply li items and real hrefs. Use non-links for unavailable actions and aria-current=page for the current page. No client-only pagination state.

components.name: empty-state
components.description: A centered empty result explanation and optional action.
components.accessibility: Use this for a real empty result, not as an error/loading substitute. The h2 assumes a page h1 already exists.

components.name: skeleton
components.description: A decorative placeholder for an explicitly labelled loading region.
components.accessibility: This is hidden from assistive technology. The caller must supply meaningful loading text and aria-busy on the actual region. No animation by default.

components.name: progress
components.description: A labelled native determinate progress indicator.
components.accessibility: Provide a meaningful label including progress if needed. Value and maximum must describe a real operation; this does not implement upload or polling.

components.name: icon
components.description: A bundled Lucide icon drawn in the current text colour.
components.accessibility: Decorative by default: without a label the icon is aria-hidden and the adjacent text carries the meaning. Give a label only when the icon stands alone and conveys information; it then becomes role="img" with that accessible name. Icons follow currentColor, mirror their direction on right-to-left pages and stay visible in forced-colours mode.

components.name: site-header
components.description: The site's top bar: brand, main navigation and actions, optionally sticky.
components.accessibility: Renders a header element (the banner landmark when it sits outside main) and wraps the nav slot in a nav labelled by navLabel. Give every nav on a page a distinct label. Below 48rem the navigation wraps under the brand instead of collapsing; use the menu component for an opt-in collapse. A sticky header can hide focused content: keep it short.

components.name: nav-link
components.description: A navigation link with a current-page state.
components.accessibility: Marks the current page with aria-current="page" as well as a visual state, so the location is not conveyed by colour alone. Use inside a labelled nav, such as the site header's nav slot.

components.name: site-footer
components.description: The site footer with an optional legal line.
components.accessibility: Renders a footer element (the contentinfo landmark when it sits outside main). Label any nav placed in it, for example aria-label="Footer", so it is distinguishable from the main navigation.

components.name: page-header
components.description: A page title with optional description, breadcrumbs and actions.
components.accessibility: Emits the page's h1: use one per page. Breadcrumbs come first in reading order, then the title, so screen-reader users hear where they are before what the page is.

components.name: section
components.description: A full-width page band with an optional h2 title and a centred content width.
components.accessibility: The title renders as an h2; nest deeper headings inside. A muted tone is decorative and never the only way content is grouped.

components.name: hero
components.description: A landing-page introduction with title, lead, actions and optional media.
components.accessibility: Emits an h1, so use it instead of a page header, not alongside one. The eyebrow is a plain paragraph before the heading. Media is presentation: give images real alt text, or alt="" when decorative.

components.name: media
components.description: A responsive image in a fixed aspect-ratio frame.
components.accessibility: alt is required: describe what the image shows, or pass alt="" when it is decorative or repeats adjacent text. The frame reserves its space before the image loads, so the page does not shift. Images load lazily and never carry information that is absent from the text.

components.name: price
components.description: A server-formatted price with an optional unit and previous price.
components.accessibility: The amount is shown exactly as the server formatted it: format currency and locale in Lua, never in the template. A previous price is struck through and preceded by visually hidden compareAtLabel text ("Was"), so it is not conveyed by the strike-through alone. Long numbers wrap instead of overflowing.

components.name: product-card
components.description: A catalogue tile that links to a product, with media, badges, price and actions.
components.accessibility: The title is an h3 link and the whole card is clickable through it: the link stretches over the card, so the card announces once, as its title. The focus ring is drawn around the card. Controls in the actions slot sit above the stretched link and stay separately clickable and focusable. Keep media decorative (alt="") when the title already names the product.

components.name: option-cards
components.description: A fieldset of large, selectable option cards backed by native radios.
components.accessibility: A real fieldset and legend group the choices, and each card is a native radio inside its label: arrow keys move between options and the form submits without JavaScript. The selected card adds a border and an inset ring as well as a tint. Give every option-card in the group the same name.

components.name: option-card
components.description: One selectable option inside option-cards: a native radio with a label, description and aside.
components.accessibility: The radio stays a native input inside its label, so the whole card is the click target and the name, description and aside are read together. A component cannot read its parent's props, so pass the shared name on every card. Disabled options stay visible and are skipped by the keyboard.

components.name: quantity-input
components.description: A native number input with enhancement-only − and + buttons.
components.accessibility: The number input is the control: it is labelled, typeable, honours min, max and step and submits without JavaScript. The runtime quantity behaviour reveals the − and + buttons, which carry translatable aria-labels and fire native input and change events. Validate the quantity again on the server.

components.name: basket-line
components.description: One basket or order line with media, details, actions and a line total; with a line it updates or removes itself.
components.accessibility: Each line is an article headed by an h3 with the product name, so screen-reader users can move line by line. Totals are preformatted by the server. With line, the row shows a labelled quantity input and Update and Remove buttons whose accessible names include the product name (visually hidden), so repeated rows stay distinct. Privileged: those buttons run the site's lib/basket.lua, which must check that the line belongs to the visitor. Without line, put edit and remove actions in the actions slot, with the same context.

components.name: buy-now
components.description: A buy-it-now button with a quantity, handing the visitor to the site's checkout.
components.accessibility: The quantity is a labelled native number input and the button a real submit button, so it works without JavaScript and from the keyboard; Enter in the quantity submits. The button's accessible name includes the product name (visually hidden), so several on one page stay distinct. Errors render in a role="alert" region. Privileged: its server export runs the site's lib/checkout.lua with the visitor's Portal access and may redirect to an https checkout page.

components.name: order-summary
components.description: A summary panel of order rows, a prominent total and checkout actions.
components.accessibility: Renders a section with an h2 title (pass title=null to supply your own heading). The total is a dt/dd pair, so it is read as "Total, £58.80". Build rows with description-list so terms and values stay associated. Totals are calculated on the server; never present a client-side estimate as the payable amount.

components.name: dialog
components.description: A native modal dialog with a trigger, title, body and footer.
components.accessibility: Uses a native dialog opened with showModal, so focus moves into it, the page behind is inert, Escape closes it and focus returns to the trigger. Supporting browsers handle the trigger and close button through invoker commands; the runtime dialog behaviour covers the rest. The trigger is enhancement-only: without JavaScript it stays hidden, so keep an ordinary page link to the same content. The trigger slot is the label inside the component's own button; the close button is labelled by closeLabel.

components.name: menu
components.description: A button that opens a native popover list of navigation links.
components.accessibility: A navigation menu, not an application menu: the trigger is a button with popovertarget and the panel is a native popover holding a list of links, so Tab moves through the links, Escape and clicking outside close it and it works without JavaScript. Where CSS anchor positioning is unsupported the panel opens centred in the viewport.

components.name: menu-item
components.description: One link inside a menu, with a current-page state.
components.accessibility: Renders a list item and an ordinary link. current marks it with aria-current="page" and a bolder weight, not colour alone. Use only inside menu.

components.name: popover
components.description: A help button that opens a short native popover.
components.accessibility: A button with popovertarget opens a native popover: Enter or Space toggles it, Escape and clicking outside close it, and it works without JavaScript. With iconOnly the label becomes visually hidden text, so the button keeps its name. Use it for supplementary help only; anything required to complete a task belongs on the page. The component is inline (span) so it can sit inside a sentence: put phrasing content in it, not paragraphs or lists.

components.name: tabs
components.description: Tabbed panels that read as stacked, headed sections without JavaScript.
components.accessibility: Without JavaScript every panel shows in order under its own heading. The runtime tabs behaviour reveals the tab buttons and adds tab, tablist and tabpanel roles, roving focus and arrow, Home and End keys. Pass tabs from loader data (object literals are not supported in bindings): one {id, title} per tab-panel, in the same order, with selected: true on the initially selected one. Mismatched sets stay unenhanced.

components.name: tab-panel
components.description: One panel inside tabs, headed by its title.
components.accessibility: Each panel is a section with an h3 title, so without JavaScript the panels read as ordinary headed sections. Once enhanced the title is visually hidden because the selected tab names the panel. The id must equal the matching tabs entry id.

components.name: description-list
components.description: Term and value pairs, stacked in a responsive grid or inline as rows.
components.accessibility: A native dl: each description-item is a div holding one dt and one dd, so assistive technology reads term and value together. Inline rows place the value at the end of the line; both layouts wrap long values instead of overflowing.

components.name: description-item
components.description: One term and its value inside description-list.
components.accessibility: Renders a div wrapping a dt and a dd, which HTML allows inside a dl. The value may be rich content such as a badge or link. Use only inside description-list.

components.name: timeline
components.description: An ordered progress timeline of done, current and upcoming steps.
components.accessibility: An ordered list labelled by label, so its length and position are announced. The current step carries aria-current="step", and every step starts with visually hidden state text (Completed, Current step, Upcoming), so state never relies on the marker colour or icon. Markers are decorative and mirror on right-to-left pages.

components.name: timeline-step
components.description: One step in a timeline: a title, an optional time and detail.
components.accessibility: Renders a list item. state=current adds aria-current="step". The state is spelled out as visually hidden text before the title; pass stateLabel to translate it (for example "Erledigt:"). Use only inside timeline.

components.name: stat
components.description: A labelled key figure with an optional change and trend.
components.accessibility: The label precedes the value in reading order. The trend arrow is decorative and coloured as a supplement: the change text must say the direction and amount itself (for example "+3 this week"). Values are preformatted by the server.

components.name: estimate-panel
components.description: A price estimate with line rows, a total that can follow a quantity live, delivery and actions.
components.accessibility: Renders a section with an h2 title and the total as a dt/dd pair. With unitPrice, a control named quantity inside the panel re-estimates the total as the visitor edits it: only the total is replaced, never the control being edited, and without JavaScript the total stays as rendered. Announce updates from a data-portal-status outlet outside the panel. The estimate is not a quote: the server recalculates the payable price.

components.name: file-list
components.description: A list of downloadable files.
components.accessibility: A list of ordinary links. Each link names the file, then its type and size, so the accessible name says what will download and how big it is. Serve files through an authorised page or Folder route; the link grants no access by itself.

components.name: file-item
components.description: One downloadable file inside file-list: name, type and size.
components.accessibility: An ordinary link with the download attribute; the icons are decorative. Use only inside file-list.

components.name: code-block
components.description: Preformatted code with a language label and a copy button.
components.accessibility: The code sits in a pre that is keyboard-focusable, so long lines can be scrolled with the arrow keys, and stays left-to-right on right-to-left pages. language is a visible label only: there is no client-side highlighting. With copy (the default) the runtime copy behaviour reveals the button, copies the text and announces copiedMessage (default "Copied"; set it alongside copyLabel to localise the control); without JavaScript the button stays hidden and the text stays selectable. Write the code flush to the start of the line: whitespace in the slot is preserved.

components.name: endpoint
components.description: An API operation heading: method, path, summary and documentation content.
components.accessibility: Renders a section headed by an h3 that reads as method then path, for example "GET /v1/orders/{reference}". The method colour comes from the status tokens and is never the only cue: the method is always written out. Paths stay left-to-right and wrap at any character instead of overflowing.

components.name: property-table
components.description: A table of API or schema properties: name, type, required and description.
components.accessibility: A captioned table with real column headers (translatable through the *Label props). Supply one tr per property with four td cells; write "Yes" or "No" for Required rather than a symbol. The labelled wrapper is keyboard-focusable so a wide table can be scrolled.

components.name: key-display
components.description: A labelled secret that shows only its masked form and copies the full value. The full value is delivered in the page source as a hidden copy source, so use it only on authenticated pages shown to the key's owner.
components.accessibility: Only masked is displayed or announced: the full value sits in a hidden copy source, so it never appears on screen or in the accessibility tree, and the copy button (revealed by the runtime copy behaviour) puts it on the clipboard and announces copiedMessage (default "Copied"; set it alongside copyLabel to localise the control). The full value is delivered in the page source (the hidden copy source), so anyone who can view the source of the page has the key: use it only on authenticated, uncached pages shown to the key's owner, mask on the server, and prefer showing a new secret once.

components.name: avatar
components.description: A round image or initials standing for a person or organisation.
components.accessibility: The avatar is an image named by name; initials and any photo inside it are hidden from assistive technology. DataXML cannot derive initials, so the caller passes them. When the name is already written next to the avatar, prefer leaving the avatar out of the reading order in your own markup.

components.name: kbd
components.description: A keyboard key or shortcut, styled as a keycap.
components.accessibility: Uses the native kbd element. Write key names out in full where they are ambiguous (for example "Ctrl"), and never make a shortcut the only way to do something.

layouts.name: layout-shop
layouts.title: Print shop
layouts.description: A public storefront: a branded hero, a bestseller grid and a product page with paper options, quantity and a live estimate.
layouts.integration: Load products and prices with a read loader and pass server-formatted amounts to price. Put the options and quantity in a GET form targeting the estimate region (data-portal-region on the wrapper, data-portal-live on the form) with a status outlet outside it; recalculate the estimate in Lua on every change. Adding to the basket is a protected Lua action. The product band is plain section markup rather than the section component because a region cannot sit inside a component slot. This static example has no form, so nothing is calculated or submitted. The product illustrations under /examples/images/ exist only in this showcase: replace them with your own asset URLs.

layouts.name: layout-ordering-portal
layouts.title: Private ordering portal
layouts.description: A signed-in B2B portal: approved items to reorder, a basket summary with an approval step, and the sign-in card visitors see first.
layouts.integration: Use your Portal authentication flow for the sign-in page; never put credentials in query strings or client storage. Scope the reorder list to the signed-in PortalUser's customer and read contract prices on the server. Basket changes and "send for approval" are protected Lua actions; group related writes in the platform transaction capability. The demo has no form or endpoint and every action is disabled. The product illustrations under /examples/images/ exist only in this showcase: replace them with your own asset URLs.

layouts.name: layout-tracking
layouts.title: Job tracking
layouts.description: An order page with a production timeline, order details, downloadable documents and a list of recent orders with status badges.
layouts.integration: Fetch the order through an authorised Lua read handler scoped to the current PortalUser and customer membership; an order reference is an identifier, not permission to view it. Map production events to timeline steps on the server. Serve documents through an authorised route or Folder binding. Tracking, totals and files here are fictional.

layouts.name: layout-api
layouts.title: API reference
layouts.description: Developer documentation: endpoints with parameter tables, copyable code samples in tabs and a masked API key with a copy button.
layouts.integration: Generate endpoints and property tables from your API description in Lua and pass tabs from loader data. Render key-display only on authorised, uncached pages, mask the key on the server and pass the full value only to the signed-in owner; prefer showing a new secret once. Copy buttons and tabs need the Portal runtime; without it every sample still shows. The key here is fictional.
